target_customer: E-commerce and logistics warehouses that pick, pack and kit orders
problem: Warehouse picking is manual labor that robots rarely handle reliably. InLoop ships imperfect policies into real warehouses, recovers automatically and calls a remote human operator when it cannot, turning failures into training data.
business_model: Robots as a service: monthly rental covering bimanual hardware, software updates and remote support, with no upfront cost (per aggregator profiles)
product_category: AI-native robotic fulfillment with teleoperation fallback

founders.name: Zakariea Sharfeddine
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a machine learning background; education not listed.

founders.name: Stepan Feduniak
founders.background_notes: YC page says robot learning research on VLA models and reinforcement learning at KIT and TUM; degrees not listed.

competitors.name: Brightpick
competitors.what: AI mobile manipulators for fulfillment; launched Gridpicker at LogiMAT in March 2026

competitors.name: Nomagic
competitors.what: AI robotic piece picking; launched Shoebox Picker in February 2026

technical_complexity.rationale: Robust bimanual manipulation with learned policies, failure detection and teleoperation handoff in real warehouses, built by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded pick and pack robotics companies exist; the claimed edge is production failure data, which is unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established vendors released new picking products in early 2026; outcome for InLoop is unknown.

market_need_then: Warehouse labor automation demand and rapid progress in robot learning models. The YC listing and aggregator profiles mention paid pilots in customer warehouses from March 2026, which is self-reported and not verified.

branding.name_origin: A profile of the founder presents the human in the loop idea as the core of the name, but no source states the etymology
branding.domain_note: Uses inloop-robotics.com, an exact name with a Robotics suffix

identity.logo: InLoop wordmark with a simple logo
identity.visual_style: Minimal layout with a Schedule a Demo call to action
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident, imperative: 'Automate Manual Labor from Day One'

branding.brand_signature: Human in the loop positioning built into the name

brand_strength.rationale: The name ties to the product's human fallback concept, but there is little press about the brand and the name is generic.

outcome_analysis: InLoop Robotics is a small Spring 2026 robotics startup with machine learning founders from Bosch and BMW and research ties. It sells robots as a monthly service and reports paid pilots. No verified funding, exit or distress was found; the outcome is too early to judge amid well-funded picking vendors.
notes: Aggregators conflict on funding: one lists a $500k pre-seed in June 2026 (FundedIQ), another about $130K seed; both unverified and not recorded. Nvidia Inception participation comes from a LinkedIn post and yespress.io, not a round. A third co-founder, Pasha Rizali, appears only on an aggregator and is not listed on the YC page, so he is not recorded. yespress.io fetch returned 403 and was not worked around. Location conflict: YC says Germany (BY), site says San Francisco. Team size 10 on YC list, 4 on profile. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed (June 2026) is recorded from FundedIQ, with VCBacked listing a June 2026 pre-seed and Y Combinator. YesPress instead reports a $130K seed in March 2026, which conflicts and is not recorded. The round rests on aggregators only.
